I'll have to disagree on two different counts:

1) Reform of refund policies on online purchases.

Companies with decent online marketplaces such as GOG and Valve have made strides towards reimbursing gamers who pre-order and receive shit, broken products on release.

The Steam Refund Policy introduced recently was likely one of the main reasons why Batman: Arkham Knight was actually pulled from Steam with a huge public apology from Warner Bros for the state it was released in. Beforehand, a lot of companies would not give two flying fucks about the state of a game once released but since it actually hampered profits generated from pre-ordering the game, it's no surprise that Warner Bros had to act.

The more reform we see towards reimbursing gamers who are shafted by the industry, the better. Especially when hiding 'on purchase, you surrender your right to a refund' in the Terms and Conditions generally leads to bad customer service.

2) Indies are the renaissance of gaming.

Indie studios are perceived to have more dedicated staff and a much nicer working atmosphere than the team of a AAA development studio, and it really shows in the work of some of these studios. They have produced some of the greatest-looking games known to man such as Shovel Knight, Freedom Planet, A Hat In Time, Minecraft, CrossCode, Zineth, Hover: Revolt of Gamers, and others.

The only thing hampering indie studios is when they get bought out by a big publisher and in turn, the quality of their products take a nosedive. Two of the best examples I can think of is when RedOctane (and the Guitar Hero franchise) got bought out by Activision, and when Vivendi and Activision merged into Activision-Blizzard.

While RedOctane and Blizzard are by no means small indie studios, the quality of future games in franchises such as Guitar Hero, Warcraft, Starcraft and Diablo plummeted.

Look at World of Warcraft now for instance with Warlords of Draenor dumbed-down to such an extent that it has about 20% of the content and depth in its gameplay mechanics as the original vanilla game. And look at Guitar Hero being so heavily milked that the franchise keeled over and died after seventeen games were released in less than four years.

And given how companies like Epic, Crytek, Enterbrain, id Software and Unity are trying to make both 2D and 3D games much easier to develop, I can only see indie games getting better and better.
